content: 1. Osimertinib: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Rifapentine and Ospemifene: Rifapentine decreases ospemifene levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Oxybutynin: Rifapentine reduces oxybutynin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Oxycodone: Rifapentine decreases oxycodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ozanimod: Co-administration is not recommended. 6. Paclitaxel: Rifapentine reduces paclitaxel levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Pacritinib: Rifapentine decreases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Palbociclib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Panobinostat: Rifapentine reduces panobinostat levels by ~70%, leading to potential treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Perampanel: Rifapentine decreases perampanel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be required, and close monitoring is necessary. 11. Pexidartinib: Rifapentine reduces pexidartinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Phenytoin: Rifapentine decreases phenytoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Pimavanserin: Rifapentine reduces pimavanserin efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible, and consider dosage adjustments. 14. Progesterone (various forms): Rifapentine reduces progesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use non-hormonal contraceptives as an alternative. 15. Quetiapine: Rifapentine decreases quetiapine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ranolazine: Rifapentine reduces ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Regorafenib: Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Rilpivirine: Rifapentine reduces rilpivirine levels, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Sildenafil: Rifapentine significantly reduces sildenafil plasma levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Simvastatin: Rifapentine reduces simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Sonidegib: Rifapentine reduces sonidegib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration. 22. Sorafenib: Rifapentine decreases sorafenib levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use an alternative drug. 23. Tacrolimus: Rifapentine reduces tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Tadalafil: Rifapentine reduces tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use in pulmonary hypertension patients and monitor erectile dysfunction patients closely. 25. Tamoxifen: Rifapentine decreases tamoxifen levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ticagrelor: Rifapentine reduces ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 27. Tramadol: Rifapentine decreases tramadol and its active metabolite levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 induction. Use an alternative drug. 28. Tucatinib: Rifapentine reduces tucatinib plasma concentrations by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Rifapentine reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Velpatasvir (with Sofosbuvir): Rifapentine reduces velpatasvir and sofosbuvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Tivozanib: Rifapentine reduces tivozanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Siponimod: Rifapentine reduces siponimod levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration, especially in patients with specific CYP2C9 genotypes. 33. Sirolimus: Rifapentine reduces sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Sunitinib: Rifapentine decreases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Toremifene: Rifapentine reduces toremifene levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Triazolam: Rifapentine reduces triazolam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tivozanib: Rifapentine reduces tivozanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Tucatinib: Rifapentine reduces tucatinib plasma concentrations by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Rifapentine reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. This list highlights the significant interactions between rifapentine and various drugs, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, or alternative therapies in many cases.
